---
title: "Compute tiers"
---

i-spi-compute can be scaled in two ways, and they solve different problems.

## More workers on one tier: throughput

One tier is one API, one Redis queue and one or more workers. Every worker
takes jobs from the same queue, so raising `replicas` on the
`i-spi-compute-worker` Deployment runs more jobs at once.

Within one worker, fits also run in parallel: the worker fits several curve
groups at the same time in child processes, each with its own database
connection. How many depends on `WORKER_CORES` and the container's memory
limit. Set `WORKER_CORES` to the container's CPU limit: the worker cannot see
the limit itself and would otherwise start more processes than it has CPUs.

## Several tiers: isolation

A second tier is a complete second copy, with its own API, queue and workers,
writing to the same database. Long jobs on one tier, such as a large
simulation, then do not hold up everyday fits on the other. A second tier also
lets a new worker release run on chosen studies before everywhere else.

I-SPI chooses the tier per project or study with the **`compute_cluster`**
setting:

- empty or `default`: the tier in `ISPI_COMPUTE_URL` / `ISPI_COMPUTE_API_KEY`;
- any other value, for example `sim`: the tier in `ISPI_COMPUTE_URL__SIM` /
  `ISPI_COMPUTE_API_KEY__SIM`.

The value is matched without regard to case, with `-` read as `_`, so `sim`,
`SIM` and `Sim` all select `__SIM`. A tier without its own API key uses the
default key. A value that matches no variable falls back to the default tier,
and I-SPI logs a warning. I-SPI reads these variables when it starts.

## Adding the optional sim tier

[`k8s-manifests/i-spi-compute-sim.yml`](https://github.com/immunoplex/i-spi-deployment/blob/main/k8s-manifests/i-spi-compute-sim.yml)
is a ready second tier. It reuses the `i-spi-compute` Secret, so it has no
Secret of its own and needs no new placeholder.

1. Apply it after `i-spi-compute.yml`:
   `sudo kubectl -n immunoplex apply -f i-spi-compute-sim.yml`
2. In `i-spi.yml`, uncomment `ISPI_COMPUTE_URL__SIM` and
   `ISPI_COMPUTE_API_KEY__SIM`, and apply it again. I-SPI restarts with the
   new variables.
3. In I-SPI's settings, set `compute_cluster` to `sim` for the projects or
   studies that should use it.

A third tier follows the same pattern: copy the file, rename every `-sim` to
`-<name>`, and add `ISPI_COMPUTE_URL__<NAME>` to `i-spi.yml`.

## Which to use

- Fits queue up and every study is equally urgent: more worker replicas, or
  larger workers.
- One kind of work should not wait behind another, or should run on separate
  hardware or a different release: a second tier.
